items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Three Indian Space Founders Who Met PM Modi Debate If India Can Lead the World in Space
items.summary:
Six years after India opened its space sector to private participation, the ecosystem is moving beyond pitch decks to operational orbital constellations. With over 440 registered space tech startups and nearly $620 million in private funding, India aims to scale its space economy to $44 billion by 2033. As ISRO transfers mature launch vehicle manufacturing like the SSLV to private industry, the country is shifting toward deep-tech hardware, precision PNT constellations, OptoSAR earth observation, and climate analytics.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with three founders who met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on National Space Day: Suyash Singh (Co-Founder & CEO, GalaxEye), Lokesh Kabdal (Co-Founder & CEO, VyomIC), and Samuel John (Founder & CEO, mistEO). They discuss key takeaways from their PM meeting, the transition of ISRO's legacy technology, building resilient domestic supply chains, moving from low-cost launching to trusted global IP, and destigmatizing failure in deep-tech experimentation.

When the world thinks space, will it think India?

items.title: Ai2: The best AI tools aren't built for scientists. They're built with them.
items.summary:
Decades of cancer data sit in repositories around the world, holding answers no one has had time to look for. This is the story of one of them — and of what happened when a AI system and a team of cancer researchers went looking together.

Working side by side, Ai2 and the Paul G. Allen Research Center at Providence Swedish Cancer Institute used AutoDiscovery to surface a hypothesis no one was asking about: that invasive lobular carcinoma, a breast cancer subtype long written off as unresponsive to immunotherapy, carries a stronger immune signature than anyone recognized. 

This is how we believe AI for science should be built — in the lab, with the scientists who will use it, held to their standards of evidence. 

The Swedish Cancer Institute is now deploying AutoDiscovery, to use on their own protected research data.
